key_insight: Solutal Marangoni stress stabilizes the falling film, thermal Marangoni stress increases peak disturbance growth, and elastic memory modifies instability onset and finite-wavelength behavior.
engineering_relevance: These competing effects can inform strategies for controlling wave growth in heated, surfactant-containing viscoelastic film processes.
method: Orr–Sommerfeld stability analysis and long-wave limit.
Five-field weighted-residual model for nonlinear evolution.
Compatible bulk–surface fluxes conserving total projected surfactant inventory in periodic domains.
evidence_signal: Numerical examples show reduced growth and nonlinear wave amplitude with solutal Marangoni stress, alongside hump-and-ripple profiles with coupled concentration and temperature variations.
watch_item: Large-elasticity results are formal predictions of the truncated short-memory model, not controlled predictions for strongly elastic flow.
paper_title: Thermosolutal Marangoni instabilities in a weakly viscoelastic falling film with soluble surfactant
